{{Short description|American chemist and academic (1936–1981}}
'''Willis H. Flygare''' (July 24, 1936 – May 18, 1981) was an American [[chemist|physical chemist]] and professor at [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/readingroom.php?book=biomems&page=wflygare.html National Academies Press, Biographical Memoirs, Willis H. Flygare, By David Chandler]</ref><ref name="UI">[http://chemistry.illinois.edu/events/lectures/flygare/about_Willis_Flygare.html Chemistry at Illinois, Flygare Memorial Lectures, About Willis H. Flygare]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?flygarew|title= Willis Flygare
|publisher=Array of Contemporary American Physicists|accessdate= May 1, 2016}}</ref>

==Background==
Flygare was born in [[Jackson, Minnesota]]. He was the son of  Willis B. and Doris H. Flygare, both of whom were of Scandinavian descent. He attended [[St. Olaf College]] in [[Northfield, Minnesota]], from which he graduated in 1958 with majors in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. He later attended graduate school at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], earning his Ph.D. in chemistry in 1961.<ref>{{cite book
|url= http://www.nap.edu/read/11429/chapter/9#137|title= Willis H. Flygare July 24, 1936–May 18, 1981|publisher=  nap.edu|author=   David Chandler  |year= 2005|doi= 10.17226/11429|isbn= 978-0-309-09304-0|accessdate=May 5, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/events/lectures/flygare/about_Willis_Flygare.html|title= About Willis H. Flygare|publisher= The Department of Chemistry at the University of Illinois|access-date= May 1, 2016|archive-date= April 13, 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160413033527/http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/events/lectures/flygare/about_Willis_Flygare.html|url-status= dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Flygare became a professor of chemistry at the [[University of Illinois]] in 1961 and stayed in that position until his premature death at age 44 of [[Lou Gehrig disease]]. Flygare is credited with "outstanding contributions to the understanding of molecular electronic structure".<ref name="UI"/>

He invented a highly sensitive pulsed-beam, [[fourier transform|Fourier-transform]] [[Microwave spectroscopy|microwave spectrometer]].<ref name="UI"/>

He also developed a new method based on the molecular [[Zeeman effect]] for measurements of  molecular [[quadrupole moment]]s and [[magnetic susceptibility]] [[anisotropies]].<ref name="UI"/>

He received [[Irving Langmuir Award]] in 1981.<ref name="NAP"/>

Flygare was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="NAP"/><ref name="UI"/>

The University of Illinois established lectures in his name and a memorial fund.<ref>[http://chemistry.illinois.edu/giving/funds/flygare.html The Department of Chemistry at the University of Illinois, The Willis H. Flygare Memorial Fund]</ref>

== Awards and distinctions ==
* [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]s in 1972 and 1978<ref name="UI"/>
* [[Phi Lambda Upsilon]] Fresenius Award in 1971<ref name="UI"/><ref>[http://philambdaupsilon.org/national-fresenius-award/award-recipients/ Phi Lambda Upsilon:Award Recipients]</ref>
* [[Baekeland]] Medal in 1973<ref name="UI"/>
* [[Irving Langmuir Award]] in 1981<ref name="UI"/>
* elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1974<ref name="UI"/>
* honorary doctorate from [[St. Olaf College]] in 1976<ref name="UI"/>
